## The exponential model {#fm6-finish .fm-slide }

$$\text{Quantity}=\text{initial quantity}\times(\text{multiplier})^{\text{number of periods}}$$

A constant percentage change gives a constant multiplier.

::: {.takeaway}
I can form an exponential rule and use it to calculate a quantity or estimate when it reaches a target.
:::

**Exit check:** what does the initial quantity tell you about the graph?

::: notes
The graph passes through the initial quantity when time is zero. In financial examples with periodic crediting, distinguish the discrete valuation points from a smooth curve used to interpolate. Ask students to explain how growth differs from decay using the multiplier.
:::
